nodes.title: The normalized lattice Weierstrass model
nodes.statement: For a native PeriodPair L, define W_L with a₁=a₂=a₃=0, a₄=−L.g₂/4 and a₆=−L.g₃/4. Its discriminant is L.g₂³−27L.g₃² and is nonzero. The projective map z↦[℘_L(z):℘′_L(z)/2:1] off the lattice extends across each lattice point by O=[0:1:0] and descends to a pointed biholomorphism C/L.lattice ≅ W_L^an. It intertwines addition with the algebraic group law.
hypotheses: The lattice has rank two over Z and spans C over R. Its orientation is not part of PeriodPair; choose an oriented basis only when normalizing to H.
Projective affine coordinates use the native Weierstrass equation y²=x³−g₂x/4−g₃/4. Totalized native ℘ values at a pole are not projective coordinates.
proofSteps: Use the native differential equation away from the lattice. Laurent expansions ℘=z⁻²+O(z²), ℘′=−2z⁻³+O(z) give the projective extension at O.

Count zeros of the elliptic function ℘−x to obtain a two-sheeted x-map and injectivity once ℘′ is included. Its three nonzero half-periods have distinct x-values; hence the cubic discriminant is nonzero.
Periodicity descends the map; compactness and the local charts show it is a biholomorphism. The explicit ℘ addition formula identifies the group laws.

nodes.title: Pointed elliptic uniformization
nodes.statement: For a smooth projective Weierstrass elliptic curve E/C with identity O, the complex analytification of AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension (its package §7.10.1) is a compact connected one-dimensional complex Lie group. There is a rank-two discrete lattice Λ⊂C and a pointed holomorphic group isomorphism C/Λ→E^an. Conversely every such lattice is realized by the preceding Weierstrass model. Isomorphisms of pointed elliptic curves correspond to nonzero homotheties uΛ=Λ′; general holomorphic group homomorphisms correspond to complex-linear maps z↦uz with uΛ⊂Λ′, including u=0. Algebraic and analytic pointed morphisms agree.
hypotheses: E is smooth, projective, geometrically connected of genus one, with its algebraic group law.
Use the projective points dictionary, not only the affine solution set.
proofSteps: Analytify the smooth projective curve and its group maps. Proper coherent comparison (properSchemeGagaPushforward in AlgebraicModuli package §7.10.3) gives H⁰(E^an,O)=C, hence connectedness, and compact-surface cohomology identifies its analytic genus as one; choose the nonzero algebraic invariant differential ω.

Integrate ω around an oriented integral homology basis. The bilinear relation and positivity of iω∧conjugate(ω) make its two periods real-linearly independent. Integration from O defines E^an→C/Λ; it is a local isomorphism since ω never vanishes. Compactness and connectedness make it a covering onto the torus. Its induced homology image is the whole period lattice by definition, hence the covering has degree one. Invariance of ω identifies the group law.

Use the explicit lattice Weierstrass map for the inverse construction. Lift pointed group maps to the universal covers; their additive holomorphic lifts are complex-linear. Proper-source morphism comparison algebraizes maps between the proper algebraic curves.

Pass to the quotients and count the kernel by the lattice index. Algebraize the pointed map using C4 and compare degrees on a finite covering.
Composition gives the isogeny and differential compatibilities; identify duals by their composite with multiplication.

nodes.title: Invariant differentials and periods
nodes.statement: Under the normalized lattice uniformization, the algebraic invariant differential dx/(2y) pulls back to dz. For any E/C and nonzero invariant differential ω, its period homomorphism H₁(E^an,Z)→C has image a full lattice Λ_ω, and integration from O gives E^an≅C/Λ_ω with ω corresponding to dz. Changing ω to cω changes the period lattice to cΛ_ω. An oriented integral homology basis gives τ=ω₂/ω₁∈H and the usual positive Riemann bilinear area.
hypotheses: Use the complex orientation on E^an and a positively oriented homology basis.
The differential line is imported from MC1C. The period map is the concrete integration map, not an arbitrary rank-two subgroup.
proofSteps: Compute dx/(2y)=d℘/℘′=dz off the finite half-period locus and extend the equality of holomorphic forms.

Pull an invariant differential back along the preceding pointed lattice uniformization; translation invariance makes it a constant nonzero multiple of dz. A lift of a homology loop ends at the corresponding lattice point, so integration identifies H₁ with the period lattice.
Positivity of iω∧ω̄ fixes the orientation; rescaling the differential gives the homothety formula.

nodes.title: The analytic Weil-pairing comparison
nodes.statement: Fix Λ=Zω₁+Zω₂ with Im(ω₂/ω₁)>0 and N≥1. With the Tau Ceti pairing e_N(S,T)=τ_S^*g_T/g_T of Silverman III.8, where g_T has divisor [N]^*(T)−[N]^*(O) and τ_S is translation X↦X+S, e_N((aω₁+bω₂)/N,(cω₁+dω₂)/N)=exp(−2πi(ad−bc)/N). This is the imported algebraic Weil pairing evaluated on the corresponding torsion sections, and is compatible with homotheties, isogenies and their duals, and change of level. In particular on Λ_τ=Z+Zτ the ordered frame (τ/N,1/N) has pairing ζ_N=exp(2πi/N), and the frame (1/N,τ/N) has pairing ζ_N⁻¹.
hypotheses: The displayed coefficients are integers interpreted modulo N.

The sign is fixed by the Tau Ceti definition e_N(S,T)=τ_S^*g_T/g_T; exchanging the roles of S and T inverts every value. Conrad’s normalization ⟨τ/N,1/N⟩=ζ_N (proof of Proposition 7.16) is the same as the Tau Ceti one; the caution there concerns Silverman’s Advanced Topics, Exercise 1.15, not the AEC III.8 divisor definition. Milne’s Lemma 8.7 uses the same frame (z/N,1/N).
The algebraic group-scheme pairing and its comparison with the equation-level pairing are MC2E inputs, not reconstructed here.
proofSteps: Identify N-torsion by the quotient (1/N)Λ/Λ.

For T=t mod Λ with λ=Nt∈Λ take g_T(z)=σ(Nz−t)σ(Nz)⁻¹exp(η(λ)z), with σ the Weierstrass sigma function and η the quasi-period homomorphism; it is Λ-periodic with divisor [N]^*(T)−[N]^*(O). Quasi-periodicity of σ gives e_N(S,T)=g_T(z+s)/g_T(z)=exp((η(λ)μ−η(μ)λ)/N) for μ=Ns.
Legendre’s relation η(ω₁)ω₂−η(ω₂)ω₁=2πi for Im(ω₂/ω₁)>0 gives e_N(ω₁/N,ω₂/N)=exp(−2πi/N); bilinearity gives every coefficient. Apply the imported algebraic isogeny and change-of-level laws.

nodes.title: The marked torus family over the upper half-plane
nodes.statement: Over H form T=(C×H)/((z,τ)∼(z+m+nτ,τ)), m,n∈Z. This is a proper smooth analytic group family with identity, and its sections P=1/N and Q=τ/N give an ordered N-torsion basis with Tau Ceti pairing e_N(P,Q)=ζ_N⁻¹, equivalently e_N(Q,P)=ζ_N. For γ=[[a,b],[c,d]]∈SL₂(Z), the algebraic row action (P,Q)γ=(aP+cQ,bP+dQ) matches the analytic right action τ·γ=(dτ+b)/(cτ+a) and the fibre isomorphism z↦z/(a+cτ). In usual left-action notation ητ=(ατ+β)/(γτ+δ), its label matrix is [[δ,β],[γ,α]].
hypotheses: τ∈H and N≥1; the right action is the usual left action of Jγ⁻¹J with J=diag(1,−1).
The quotient uses a sheaf of holomorphic functions descended along the lattice covering; it is not merely a topological orbit set.
Base change of the family is analytic; the general relative torus and period machinery is imported from A5.
proofSteps: On compact subsets of H, real independence bounds lattice vectors away from zero; lattice translations act freely and locally discretely, giving holomorphic quotient charts.

Use a varying fundamental parallelogram to prove properness and smoothness. Joint ℘ functions away from the relative lattice, and their projective extensions, identify the family with varying Weierstrass models.

nodes.title: Open modular uniformization with the specified level
nodes.statement: The marked torus family induces an isomorphism from the supplied analytic quotient curve to the analytification of the imported algebraic open modular curve: Γ(N)\H→Y(N,ζ_N)^an for a fixed pairing, through τ↦(C/Λ_τ,(τ/N,1/N)) (the frame (1/N,τ/N) of the marked family has pairing ζ_N⁻¹ and lands in Y(N,ζ_N⁻¹)), Γ₁(N)\H→Y₁(N)^an, and Γ₀(N)\H→Y₀(N)^an. Interpret the first as a fine curve for N≥3 and the second for N≥4; at smaller levels and for Γ₀ use the coarse quotient with its stabilizer charts. Strict full ordered level is the disjoint union of φ(N) pairing components over C, with one such quotient for each primitive pairing value. These isomorphisms identify the corresponding local families on rigidified charts.
hypotheses: N≥1 and the base is C. Full ordered level, a fixed pairing and a projective frame are three separate moduli problems.
The algebraic models and representability are MC5A/5B/9D/9E inputs; Γ₀ uses cyclic subgroups and always has generic [−1] inertia.
The target statement is an isomorphism of complex analytic curves, including their structure sheaves, not only a bijection of complex points.
proofSteps: Classify elliptic curves and their torsion labels by R12.1; changing a marking gives precisely the displayed congruence stabilizer. This supplies the point bijection.

For a local analytic family with a marking, A5 gives holomorphic period coordinates. The Weierstrass presentation and analytified étale rigidifier show that the forward map and the local inverse are holomorphic on fine charts.

For coarse cases choose an auxiliary prime-to-N full level ≥3, perform the fine comparison there, and descend finite quotient charts using stabilizer-equivariance. Do not infer local isomorphism from point bijectivity.

nodes.title: Generalized elliptic curves
nodes.statement: A generalized elliptic curve E/S is a semistable genus-one curve with a commutative S-group structure on Eˢᵐ and an action Eˢᵐ×_S E→E extending translation on Eˢᵐ. nodes.title: The translation structure criterion
nodes.statement: Let C/S be semistable genus one with section e in Cˢᵐ. If a commutative flat locally finitely presented S-group G acts on C, acts trivially on the algebraic space Pic⁰_{C/S} and, on every geometric fibre, transitively on the irreducible components, then C has a unique generalized elliptic structure with identity e for which G acts by translations. nodes.title: Fine loci and bad-level inertia
nodes.statement: The compact full-level stack over Z is a fine scheme for N≥2 unless N is a prime power p^s or twice a prime power 2p^s; N=1 is an additional nonfine case. In the exceptional bad fibres there can be nontrivial automorphisms preserving a Drinfeld full set. A sufficient fine condition for compact Γ₁(N) over a base is that N have an invertible divisor d≥5 on that base; the open complex fine range N≥4 is not substituted at cusps. On an m-gon with an ample naive cyclic order-N subgroup, the relative scaling inertia is μ_gcd(m,N/m), commuting with inversion. Thus naive Γ₀(N) is DM over Z exactly for squarefree N. For arbitrary mixed Γ₁(N;n), deleting boundary fibres at primes with v_p(n)≥v_p(N)+2 gives a DM open; if v_p(n)≤v_p(N)+1 for every p, the forgetful map to X(1) is representable and the whole stack is DM. This includes N=n=p² and corrects the older “n squarefree” criterion.
